publication.title: Vertical Context of Geographic Locations: An Empirical Comparison of Three Visualization Approaches

source_reading.scope: Identity, introduction, data/model and prototype, study design/procedure/results, limitations and availability (§§1–7); detailed appendix tables not fully extracted.

adjudication.basis: VerticalGeoVis implements geographic-entity attribute inspection using DBpedia RDF data and compares three visual approaches with18 participants. It deliberately removes relation links and flattens attributes to literals; cross-entity traversal is future work, while real KG-instance information remains the exploration object.

studies.population: 6 women/12 men; own13–27 inch single-screen laptops
studies.cohort_note: Cross-report participant overlap is not established.
studies.response_note: 18 observations per approach;9 per attribute level, not additional participants.
studies.design: Within-subject/counterbalanced three visual approaches and task order
tasks: Three task variants/person; attribute levels60,90,105,140,180,200; five value/category questions per task.
studies.results: Techniques broadly comparable for many task/attribute combinations; circular treemap receives stronger enjoyment/usefulness/satisfaction ratings.
limitations: Small homogeneous sample; many pairwise comparisons; attribute levels and question types affect outcomes; no blanket performance superiority.

descriptions.interaction: Search/select city, dataset and visual approach; scroll/pan/zoom thematic categories and inspect location attribute values.
descriptions.guidance: Thematic categories and unambiguous location/context coupling.
descriptions.backend: DBpedia N-triples and UBA JSON attributes, cleaned/postprocessed
